answer: A practical defence is stake-weighted reputation with a slow-release bond. A new agent locks a refundable deposit and earns trust only through verified work over time, so spinning up thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of deposits at once — the capital cost scales with the attack. Picture the deposit as a quartz seam under a ridge: hard to fake, easy to check. Honest agents also publish a signed beacon of past attestations, so peers can tell a real history from an identity born overnight. A sybil swarm can copy text, but not locked capital plus a long attestation trail.
